clue.text: Band won, after three knockout performances, perhaps

definitions.text: Band won, after three knockout performances, perhaps

parts.words: Band won, after three knockout performances, perhaps
parts.note: a boxing championship belt that a fighter keeps outright after winning three title bouts in the same weight class

explanation.surface: A musical group earns a prize after three stunning gigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' and 'performances' suggest music, but the band is a belt and the knockouts are in a boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: This British boxing championship trophy becomes the holder's own property after three successful title fights.

clue.text: Reasonable American who's served in pub

indicators.note: the soldier is placed in the pub as if serving there, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a local is a nearby pub that regulars frequent
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A sensible American who once worked behind a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served in' looks like working behind the bar, but it is the container signal: the soldier is placed inside the pub word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reasonable is sensible and follows sound reasoning.

clue.text: Bottle stored in inner vestibule

indicators.note: the letters are kept within the run of the words that follow, like goods put in storage

explanation.surface: A bottle is kept in a house's inner hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a container, but it means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage, the same as daring or pluck.

clue.text: Is father to fulminate after daughter brings dishonour?

indicators.note: the pieces before this word in the clue come later in the answer, following the daughter

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to fulminate is to protest furiously, to rage

explanation.surface: Is a father right to rant when his daughter disgraces the family?
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage someone is to belittle or discredit them, bringing them into disrepute.

clue.text: Opening in the French style, with a cacophony

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
a din is a loud discordant noise

explanation.surface: An overture in the French manner, played with a lot of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the French style' is surface padding around LE, the French for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction that leads into a main piece, such as a broadcast or speech, is its opener.

clue.text: Sweeper must collect everything in dance hall

indicators.note: the sweeping tool gathers up the other word, holding it inside itself

parts.note: a broom is a sweeping brush
all means everything

explanation.surface: A cleaner has to gather everything up in the dance hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A large room built for formal dancing is a dance venue.

clue.text: Litres always available in bar

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for litre or litres
ever means always, as in ever-ready

explanation.surface: Litres of drink are on tap at all hours in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is a crowbar or handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar used to prise or shift something is a crowbar, a simple machine.

clue.text: Player fighting to protect partner at table? That's okay

parts.note: S is South, one of the four players at bridge

indicators.note: the fighting surrounds the partner, guarding it inside

parts.note: action means fighting, as in troops seeing action
N is North, South's partner at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A card player battles to defend a partner at the table, and it's approved.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge the players are North, South, East and West, with North and South as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanction is an official approval, the formal saying-so that something is permitted.

clue.text: Take one's time to get fit?

definitions.meaning: to ... is to dawdle or delay
to fit in or be suited to a place

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means delay; as one it means to fit in where one is accepted.

clue.text: Runs into ice, say — cause of complaints

indicators.note: the runs go inside the jewels

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds, an example of gems
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone slides on the ice and ends up grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaints' sounds like grumbling, but it means illnesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Microbes bring on illnesses, which are complaints in the medical sense.

clue.text: Moderate patriarch in a recent case

indicators.note: the patriarch sits inside the phrase that follows, which forms the case around him

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in the late news
Levi was a son of Jacob, a Hebrew patriarch

explanation.surface: A moderate church elder involved in a recent lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' finishes the picture: A LATE is the case that holds LEVI. 'Moderate' is the verb, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To moderate pain or worry is to ease or lessen it.

clue.text: Knight in force almost smothered by comfort

indicators.note: the second piece is wrapped up inside the first, like something under a blanket

parts.note: to cheer is to comfort or encourage

indicators.note: the phrase loses its final letter, stopping just short

parts.note: a law in force is valid

explanation.surface: A knight in armour is nearly suffocated by luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' could tempt you toward chess or the letter N; here it is a French title, and 'almost' drops the last letter of the 'in force' word before the comfort word surrounds it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevalier is a French knight or cavalier.

clue.text: Lines from clergyman's address the right thing to read?

indicators.note: the lines are taken away from the clergyman's home

parts.note: a rectory is the house where a ... lives
RY is the abbreviation for railway, often clued as lines

explanation.surface: Lines from a vicar's sermon are the right thing to read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a speech, but it is a home.
explanation.definitionFit: The right-hand page of an open book is the one read on that side.

clue.text: Deadly obstacle at front of passage one left out

indicators.note: the obstacle stands before the passage in the answer

parts.note: a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

indicators.note: one letter is dropped from the passage

parts.note: a hall is a passage or corridor
L is the abbreviation for left, and only one of the two is removed

explanation.surface: A fatal hurdle at the start of a corridor, with one person left outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deadly is fatal, able to kill.

clue.text: Guide taking, a tourist initially — into place of worship

indicators.note: the article and the first letter go inside the building

parts.note: a temple is a building for worship

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A guide shows a tourist into a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guide' looks like a tour guide, but it is a pattern to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern used as a model for making copies.

clue.text: Connection made by Heather following successful move

indicators.note: the heather comes after the successful move in the answer

parts.note: a coup is a successful stroke or bold move
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: A link forged by a woman called Heather after a clever stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupling is a joint or link between two things, such as railway carriages.

clue.text: Chemical that's hot, perhaps, not right to mix

indicators.note: the letters are stirred together into a new order
the word for right is excluded from the preceding word

explanation.surface: A chemical that may be hot should not be mixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not right' removes R from PERHAPS, giving PEHAPS; 'to mix' then shuffles HOT and PEHAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A phosphate is a salt of phosphoric acid, a chemical compound used in fertilisers.

clue.text: Humiliate forces of disorder

indicators.note: the words are thrown into disarray, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Riot troops put the protesters to shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forces of disorder' reads as a phrase for rioters; 'disorder' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To score off someone is to get the better of them and make them look foolish.

clue.text: Business force to be established around 2000

indicators.note: the word for force goes around the number

parts.note: to coerce is to force
MM is 2000 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A company is set to be founded around the year 2000.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be established' is surface padding, a link between the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is trade, the buying and selling that makes up business.

clue.text: Carpenter's shop

definitions.meaning: British slang for a carpenter; 's stands for is

explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the same word for a woodworker and a fried-food takeaway.

clue.text: Temporary sanctuary for fighter in tricky situation

definitions.meaning: a boxer rests between rounds in a spot of the ring
to be in a tight spot is to be in a difficult position

explanation.definitionFit: A boxer's resting place between rounds and a tight spot share one word.

clue.text: Call for raising of standard? On the contrary

definitions.text: Call for raising of standard? On the contrary

parts.words: Call for raising of standard? On the contrary
parts.note: a military bugle call sounded at sunset when the flag is lowered, the opposite of raising it

explanation.surface: A summons to hoist the flag, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' also hints at a summons to raise standards of behaviour; it is a bugle call.
explanation.definitionFit: This bugle call at sunset marks the lowering of the colours, as well as meaning withdrawal.

clue.text: Gully caught anybody executing cut

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the word is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: anyone means anybody

explanation.surface: A man caught in a ravine was performing a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gully' and 'cut' suggest cricket; gully is a deep ravine here.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep narrow valley, a large gully or gorge.

clue.text: Member of extended family practising at the bar?

definitions.meaning: a relative by marriage, such as a spouse's parent

explanation.definitionFit: A relative by marriage, and, as two words, one working as a lawyer.

clue.text: Colourless people in our group without success

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the group goes around the success

parts.note: we means people in our group
a hit is a success

explanation.surface: Dull people in our circle, never succeeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: White is the absence of any colour, as in a blank page.

clue.text: Cut with something sharp and put back in place

parts.note: to reap is to cut a crop
a point is a sharp tip

explanation.surface: Someone trims with a blade and puts the thing back where it was.
explanation.definitionFit: To reappoint someone is to restore them to a post they held.

clue.text: It's silly to deny "Society", very silly

indicators.note: the society is refused a place and taken out of the word

parts.note: insane can mean extremely foolish

explanation.surface: It's foolish to reject high society; that would be very silly.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means pointless or foolish.

clue.text: Endowment's a tidy twenty-five quid at the outside

indicators.note: the sum of money goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
trim means neat and tidy

explanation.surface: An inheritance is a nice sum, twenty-five pounds at most.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tidy' suggests a tidy sum, but TRIM is tidy and A is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrimony is property inherited from one's father, an inherited endowment.

clue.text: North American's horse bolting quickly

indicators.note: the horse runs off, so it leaves the word

parts.note: the Apache are a Native American people
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A Native American's horse is galloping away fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like a steed; it is drug slang for heroin, H.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means swiftly, at a fast pace.

clue.text: Looking after number one could make leftist sneer

indicators.note: the letters could be remade into something else

explanation.surface: Selfishness might turn a left-winger into a scoffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-interest is concern for one's own advantage, putting oneself first.
